title: Beyond the beak
hook: A hidden prey item can be beyond beak reach.

knows: Birds have body structures and interact with their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: The schematic shows the tongue extending past the beak into the tunnel. Tongue length and surface features vary among woodpeckers; the diagram illustrates reach and is not a scale model.

misconception: The observed arrangement has a different effect than the one shown.
objective: An insect lies deep inside a narrow wood tunnel. Which structure can extend into the tunnel after a woodpecker opens it?

claims.text: A hidden prey item can be beyond beak reach. An insect lies deep inside a narrow wood tunnel. Which structure can extend into the tunnel after a woodpecker opens it? The schematic shows the tongue extending past the beak into the tunnel. Tongue length and surface features vary among woodpeckers; the diagram illustrates reach and is not a scale model.
claims.source: Unverified research starting point: OpenStax Biology 2e, Birds, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/29-4-birds; species- or claim-specific citations require independent matching.

claims.text: The stage is a simplified schematic and the scenario is stipulated rather than observed.
In a model of an insect deep in a crevice, what extends beyond the beak to reach it? The tongue can extend into a narrow opening beyond the beak.
